jobs.occupation: PhD Research Fellowship in Circular Battery Strategies
jobs.description:
About the position
Center for Research on Digitalization and Sustainability (CREDS), part of Inland School of Business and Social Sciences, University of Inland Norway (INN), invites candidates to apply for a three-year PhD research fellowship. The position is connected to the field of innovation studies with a specific focus on sustainability transitions, circular economy, business model change and value chains related to electric vehicle (EV) batteries in the context of energy storage and mobility. This may include research on the circular resource flows, reuse and recycle strategies, and competing end-of-life pathways for batteries and battery materials. 

Admission to INN's PhD program, Innovation in Services in the Public and Private Sectors (INSEPP), is a condition for employment as a research fellow. The candidate is expected to participate actively in INSEPP’s activities. After commencement, the candidate must apply for admission to the PhD programme within three months. An agreement for admission to the PhD programme must be in place within six months after commencement. 

As a PhD research fellow, you will be an integral part of CREDS and actively contribute to one or both of its research groups. In addition, the candidate will be employed at a department of the Business School. The position preferably commences as soon as possible, and will conclude with the award of the Degree of Doctor upon successfully completing the program. 

The position is based at CREDS in Innlandet Science Park in Kongsvinger. A high degree of on-site presence is expected. 

For further information, please contact: 

• CREDS Professor Johan Kask, +47 62 43 01 82, johan.kask@inn.no  
• CREDS Director and Professor Bård Tronvoll, +47 90 78 55 68, bard.tronvoll@inn.no  
• Head of INSEPP PhD Program Marit Engen, +47 61 28 81 07, marit.engen@inn.no About the project
Project overview 

The PhD research fellow will join an international team of researchers at CREDS, Inland School of Business and Social Sciences. We seek a highly motivated candidate to research circular battery strategies and future applications from a business and innovation perspective. CREDS’s overarching academic objective is accelerating research on the transitions enabling sustainable businesses and societies. The primary focus is to understand transitions at the level of ecosystems and markets and at the intersection between digitization and sustainability, for instance linked to new or changed business models, value chains and practices. 

The candidate’s PhD project should address how scarce resources in circular value chains related to energy and mobility are organized and governed across competing end-of-life pathways. Relevant topics include sustainable value creation, reuse and repair strategies, recycling systems, and business models that extend the useful life of batteries and battery materials. The project may examine how such arrangements work in practice, how they develop over time, and how different pathways can be assessed in relation to sustainability, loop extension, efficiency, resilience, and other relevant criteria. It may also focus on market formation, ecosystem dynamics, governance arrangements, power relations, and the role of technology in handling resource tensions across systems, as well as on how firms and other actors develop circular strategies under competing demands, regulatory change, and uncertainty about future resource use. One particularly relevant empirical example is end-of-life EV batteries, where tensions may arise between reusing or repurposing batteries for second-life energy storage and recycling materials back into battery production or other industrial uses. Norway provides a promising context for studying such issues due to its early and extensive adoption of battery-electric vehicles. 

Candidates are encouraged to define their own research design within this theme. This includes developing the specific research questions, theoretical perspective, empirical focus, and methodological approach in dialogue with the supervisory team and the academic environment at CREDS. A broad range of methodological approaches is relevant for the theme, including qualitative case studies, optimization models, system dynamics modelling, and agent-based modelling. Please note that the project may later be modified in accordance with the supervisors’ advice and the academic research agenda of CREDS. The successful candidate will have a primary supervisor among CREDS’ academic staff.
Qualifications
• The candidate must have a master’s degree and thesis on a relevant topic. Relevant academic backgrounds may include business and management, innovation studies, energy systems, industrial ecology, system dynamics, systems modelling, sustainability transitions, science and technology studies, topic-related forms of engineering, and other related interdisciplinary fields. 
• The master's degree must normally constitute 120 ECTS credits. INN’s PhD regulations require that the qualifying education includes a master’s thesis of 30 ECTS. As a rule, the average grade at master’s level must be B. 
• The qualifying degree(s) must be awarded from institutions in Norway, the EU/EEA or Switzerland, or from an international institution accredited by AACSB, AMBA and/or EQUIS. Where applicable, candidates should specify such accreditation in the application.
• Candidates who have not yet obtained the master’s degree at the time of application may apply. In this case, candidates must have submitted their master’s thesis by the application deadline. Temporary transcripts and the master’s thesis must be submitted with the application. The final diploma must be available by the time of employment. 
• Candidates with a master’s degree from a university abroad must attach “Recognition of foreign higher education” from NOKUT. Instructions for obtaining this assessment are available from NOKUT, https://hkdir.no/en/foreign-education/education-from-outside-ofnorway/recognition-of-foreign-higher-education-bachelor-master-and-phd . 
• Since the project is likely to involve extensive empirical research, dialogue with practitioners, meetings, and field-based data collection involving Norwegian and other Nordic actors, the ability to work effectively in Nordic industry and institutional contexts will be important. Relevant professional experience from industry or other practice-based settings in the Nordics, or in a comparable context, is therefore considered a strong merit. 
• Oral and written English is required. Applicants from non-English speaking countries must document their English proficiency in accordance with the Supplementary Regulations for Admission to the PhD Programme at INN University. A command of a Scandinavian language is a strong merit. 
• Expertise in relevant ICT software for research is an advantage. 
• Research experience acquired after completion of the master’s degree is considered an advantage, but is not required. 
• The candidate must be able to work independently and purposefully, and engage confidently with external actors to carry out empirical fieldwork. The role also requires the ability to collaborate well on academic research and publishing.
Evaluation of candidates for the position will be based on a total assessment of educational background, experience and personal suitability, as well as motivation and other eligibility requirements, as defined in the advertisement. In addition, the following will be emphasized: quality of the project description, documented independent research and development work or experience relevant to the project.

The position and associated tasks must be carried out in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations for government employees, including also the Act on Control of the Export of Strategic Goods, Services and Technology, etc. Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, come into conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to take up the position at University of Inland Norway. Necessary approvals must be maintained throughout the employment relationship.
How to apply
Relevant applications will be considered by an expert committee. The application and all attachments are to be submitted electronically and must include the following: 

• The applicant must submit a project proposal with a progress plan (in Norwegian or English, 5-7 pages) that explains how the research work will be carried out and addresses academic relevance, challenges and possibilities within the project. The PhD research fellow hired will, in collaboration with a supervisor, prepare a complete project proposal creating the basis for admission to the PhD program. The project proposal plays an important part in evaluating applicants and must show how the project will lead to a successful completion of a doctoral degree within three years. 
• Application letter 
• CV (summarizing education, job positions, and academic work) 
• Other work that is relevant for the application 
• Certified copies of transcripts and diplomas for the whole bachelor and master’s degree. An English translation of all education documents is required unless the documents are in Norwegian/Scandinavian. 
• Names and contact information of at least 2 reference persons. 
• A copy of the master’s thesis (in PDF)
Attachments must be uploaded as separate files. If the attachments exceed 30 MB, they must be compressed prior to upload. It is the applicant's responsibility to ensure that all attachments are uploaded. Documents submitted after expiry of the deadline will not be considered in the evaluation of your application.
We offer
• An academically stimulating and supportive work environment at a developing institution. 
• Possibility of professional development in an exciting academic research environment. 
• Position is paid and placed in position code PhD candidate 1017 in the Government Salary Scale. 
• Membership in the Norwegian Public Service Pension, with among other things, good pension and insurance schemes.
For more information about INN University as an employer, please see here.
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F0FVnszhpJYGeneral information
INN believes that there is strength in inclusion and diversity. We desire employees with different competencies, professional combinations, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to an even better way of solving problems. We will facilitate for employees who need assitance to realise their goals. Relevant adaptations can be, for example, technical aids, adapting furniture or adjusting routines, work tasks and working hours.

If there are qualified applicants with disabilities, gaps in the CV or immigrant background, we shall call at least one applicant in each of these categories for an interview. In order to be considered as an applicant in these groups, the applicants must meet certain requirements. You can read more on this here: https://arbeidsgiver.difi.no/positivsaerbehandling.

We encourage applicants to tick in Jobbnorge if they have a disability, a gap in their CV or immigrant background. The ticks in the jobseeker portal form the basis for anonymised statistics that all state-owned enterprises report in their annual reports

Information about applicants may be made public even if the applicant has asked not to be named on the list of persons who have applied. The applicant must be notified if the request to be omitted is not met.

jobs.description:
Global Test Engineer / Technician – Production test 

We are looking for a technically skilled and independent colleague to support our production sites around the world in testing, test processes, training, and follow-up activities. 

The position involves extensive travel and extended stays at our production sites. The core responsibility is to train and guide local personnel, ensure that testing is carried out in accordance with our procedures, and contribute to consistent, high-quality standards across all locations. 

You will work hands-on with test stations and equipment, provide technical support when issues arise, and ensure that local teams understand both how tests are performed and how the equipment is operated and maintained. 

Key Responsibilities 

• Travel to production sites worldwide and support local teams in performing tests and following established test processes. 
• Train and guide operators and technical personnel in test methodologies, operation of test stations, equipment, and software. 
• Ensure that testing is performed in accordance with established procedures, specifications, and quality requirements. 
• Support the installation, commissioning, and implementation of test equipment and test processes at new and existing production sites. 
• Troubleshoot, install, verify, and maintain test stations and associated equipment. 
• Document faults, deviations, and solutions, and follow up on corrective actions. 
• Collaborate with central engineering teams and technical specialists when issues require specialized expertise. 
• Prepare and configure PCs, standardized system images, and test software, and assist with basic network troubleshooting. 
• Develop and improve test instructions, user manuals, and training materials. 
• Share experiences and lessons learned from production sites with central testing, development, and engineering teams, contributing to more robust and standardized test setups. 
Qualifications and Requirements  

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent technical education in electrical engineering, automation, electronics, mechatronics, control systems, IT, or a related field. Relevant qualification combined with extensive practical experience in production, testing, technical service, or industrial environments may be considered equivalent to higher education. 
• Good technical understanding of test equipment and production processes, with a systematic approach to troubleshooting. 
• Familiarity with PCs, software installation, and standardized system configurations, as well as a basic understanding of networking. 
• Interest in IT/OT systems and how production IT supports testing and manufacturing operations. 
• Ability to follow technical procedures and quality requirements. 
• Good written and verbal communication skills in both Norwegian and English. English is the primary working language in our global projects. 
• To be considered for the position, you must be eligible to obtain a security clearance in accordance with the Norwegian Security Act.
Experience in a production environment, technical testing, or working with test equipment is an advantage, as is previous experience in technical training or travel-based technical support roles. 

You do not need to be an IT/OT or networking specialist. What matters most is that you are comfortable with hands-on troubleshooting and enjoy learning new systems and technologies. 

Personal Qualities 

You have strong communication and training skills, enjoy sharing knowledge, and are able to explain technical processes clearly and effectively. You work independently, take initiative, and approach challenges in a calm, solution-oriented, and methodical way, even when working on your own in the field. With a hands-on and practical approach, you enjoy working directly with technical equipment and solving practical technical challenges. You are structured and organized, follow established procedures, and ensure accurate documentation of your work. You are also adaptable and culturally aware, with the ability to build strong working relationships across different cultures, teams, and locations. As the role involves frequent international travel and extended stays at production sites abroad, you must be comfortable with both. 
Location: Kongsberg. The role involves a significant amount of travel.
What We Offer 

This is a varied and hands-on technical role with extensive international exposure, offering the opportunity to work with test equipment, production processes, and technical solutions across multiple countries. You will play a key role in training colleagues and ensuring consistent testing quality across our global production sites, while working closely with production, testing, IT, and engineering teams. The role also offers excellent opportunities for professional development, as well as the chance to influence and improve testing processes and working methods. 

 

About Us 

Division Missiles & Aerostructures is part of Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace. We develop, assemble, test, and deliver advanced missile systems for naval vessels, coastal defense systems, helicopters, and fighter aircraft. 

Increasing activity and international demand are driving significant growth across our missile business and production organization. Expanding production capacity across locations requires us to develop and transfer critical manufacturing expertise effectively and consistently. 

 

Important Information 

Candidates applying for this position will undergo a background check as part of the recruitment process. The outcome will be considered as part of the overall assessment. 

To be considered for the position, you must be eligible to obtain a security clearance in accordance with the Norwegian Security Act. 

Please note that the recruitment process will continue in January.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship within Predictive Runtime Verification of AI-enabled Robotic Autonomous Systems
jobs.employer_name: NORGES MILJØ- OG BIOVITENSKAPELIGE UNIVERSITET (NMBU) CAMPUS ÅS
jobs.description:
About the position
A PhD position is available in the Robotics Group at the Faculty of Science and Technology.

The PhD position is for a period of 3 years, with a desired start date of 1st of January 2026.

Recent advances in AI and Large Language Models (LLMs) bring major challenges regarding safety, uncertainty management, accountability, and runtime assurance in autonomous robotic systems. Operating in safety-critical, highly complex, dynamic, and hostile environments require systems to maintain formal safety guarantees while optimizing operational efficiency.

As a selected candidate for the announced PhD position, you will research and develop novel, context-aware, AI-enabled Predictive Runtime Verification (PRV) frameworks and adaptive monitors. By anticipating anomalies or failures before they occur, your research will enable proactive corrective actions and real-time replanning in robotic autonomous systems.

The PhD position is part of the research project PREVAIL - Predictive Runtime Verification of AI-enabled Systems, funded by the Research Council of Norway (RCN). The project builds upon scientific foundations established in the RoboFarmer project and is conducted in close strategic partnership with the Norwegian Defence University College (FHS) who will also serve as co-supervisor for the candidate and provide opportunity for research stay at FHS.
 
In addition, the PhD work will provide ample opportunity to conduct research in collaboration with international academic partners, most notably at Académie Militaire de Saint-Cyr Coëtquidan, France, University of York, UK and Royal Institute of Technology (KTH) in Stockholm, Sweden. The PREVAIL project will encourage the selected PhD candidate and provide opportunities to benefit intellectually from interaction and extended visits with internationally recognized researchers and institutes.

This PhD position is funded through the Research Council of Norway's call Supplementary Funding for Ongoing Projects to Enhance Knowledge and Results Transfer from ICT Research to the Defence Sector. The funding scheme requires candidates to be eligible for security clearance at a minimum level of "Secret". As the project is expected to involve research subject to Norwegian export control regulations, appointment is contingent upon the successful candidate obtaining the required security clearance and any necessary export control licences or approvals.
Main tasks
• Survey state-of-the-art AI-enabled Predictive Runtime Verification (PRV) methodologies and analyze their suitability for defence-oriented, safety-critical, autonomous robotic applications. 
• Formulate and develop novel algorithms, formal methodologies, and tools for context-aware PRV and AI-enhanced monitor synthesis.
• Conduct a research stay at the Norwegian Defence University College (FHS) to align research with the domain-specific requirements and preferences.
• Integrate PRV frameworks with adaptive risk-mitigation, failure avoidance, and real-time replanning mechanisms.
• Perform early-phase prototyping, software implementation (e.g., ROS 2), and testing on robotic platforms in defence-relevant environments and scenarios.
• Author scientific papers for presentation at international high-impact conferences and peer-reviewed journals.
• Complete mandatory PhD coursework and seminars in accordance with NMBU doctoral regulations.Competence
Required qualifications

• A Master's degree or equivalent in Robotics, Computer Science, Cybernetics, Formal Methods, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related field. Foreign degrees must correspond with the admission criteria for the PhD program. Candidates submitting M.Sc. thesis within the application deadline may be considered.
• In the Master’s degree, both the average grade point and the Master’s thesis, must be B or better in the Norwegian educational system. Applicants who have recently graduated with excellent results may be given preference.
• Proficiency in both written and oral English in correspondence with the admission criteria for the PhD program.
• Solid knowledge and background in at least two of the following fields: Formal Methods / Runtime Verification, AI / Machine Learning, Autonomous Systems / Control, or Software Development for Robotics (e.g., ROS/ROS 2). 
• Strong programming skills (Python, C++, etc.) 
• The successful candidate must be eligible for security clearance at a minimum level of "Secret" and any licences or approvals required under Norwegian export control legislation
• Personal suitability and motivation for the position.
Qualifications considered an advantage

• Experience with formal verification, model-checking, runtime monitoring, and/or temporal logic synthesis. 
• Experience with AI models, Large Language Models (LLMs), or reinforcement learning integrated into robotic control loops.
• Experience with safety assurance, risk analysis, adaptive systems, or research involving real-world autonomous applications.
• Practical experience working with physical mobile robotic hardware, sensors, and simulation environments.
• Previous research and peer-reviewed publications within these domains.
Personal qualities

• Be curios, result-oriented and highly motivated
• Possess strong communication and cooperation skills
• Have a solid interest in robotics
• Good collaboration skills and an ability to join interdisciplinary academic/industrial communitiesRemuneration and further information
Salary in position as PhD Research Fellow, position code 1017, 550 800 NOK. For exceptionally well qualified candidates a higher salary may be considered. 

By applying, the candidate confirms that information and documentation submitted via the job application may also be used by NMBU in a possible admission process to the PhD program. Admission to a PhD program is a prerequisite for appointment to the PhD position.

For professional and social interactions, the candidate is expected to be physically present at NMBU on a daily basis.
 
Employment is to be made in accordance with Regulations to the Universities and University Colleges Act and Regulations for the PhD degree at the Norwegian University of Life Science (NMBU) , and in accordance with the Civil Servant Act, the Security Act, and the Export Control Act. 

Appointment is contingent upon the candidate obtaining the required security clearance and any licences or approvals required under Norwegian export control legislation.

For further information, please contact Associate Professor: David Anisi (main supervisor), e-mail: david.anisi @nmbu.no.

jobs.description:
Do you want to build and lead the team that will develop and transfer missile production expertise across KONGSBERG's global manufacturing network? 

We are looking for an experienced and ambitious Team Manager to establish and lead our new Global Missile Production Training department within Strategic Production, Division Missiles & Aerostructures (DMA). 

As our global production footprint expands, developing people and transferring critical production expertise across sites will be essential to our continued growth. 

You will build the team and establish a scalable approach to production training for Naval Strike Missile (NSM) and Joint Strike Missile (JSM) in Norway and internationally. You will lead a multidisciplinary team with expertise in missile assembly, painting, inspection, testing, and technical support. 

Your Mission 

Your primary mission is to establish Global Missile Production Training as a high-performing team and a trusted partner to our production organization. You will lead by example, creating an environment where people take ownership, share expertise, collaborate effectively, and continuously improve. 

You will: 

• Build, lead, and develop a multidisciplinary production training team. 
• Recruit and develop skilled employees and create a strong culture of trust, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. 
• Plan and coordinate training activities in Norway and across international production sites. 
• Translate production needs and growth ambitions into competence requirements, training priorities, and resource plans. 
• Work closely with production management and subject-matter experts to develop and continuously improve training programs, materials, methods, and processes. 
• Drive standardization and effective knowledge transfer across locations while maintaining production and quality requirements. 
• Manage staffing, capacity, competence, and resources. 
• Build strong relationships with production leaders and stakeholders across disciplines and international sites. 
• Monitor progress, risks, and capability gaps and communicate priorities and challenges to management. 
• Ensure compliance with relevant requirements and regulations, in Norway and internationally. 
International travel will be an important part of the role. During periods of lower training demand, the team will support missile production in Norway, maintaining a strong connection between training expertise and hands-on production experience. 

Who We Are Looking For 

We are looking for a leader who combines strong people leadership, operational understanding, and the ambition to build something new. 

You understand that competence is a critical production capability and that successful industrial growth depends on our ability to develop people and transfer knowledge effectively across teams, cultures, and locations. jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
Studies of the microstructural origin of ductility in recycled aluminium alloys 

The position is a 3-year doctoral research fellowship starting in the autumn of 2027. The PhD candidate will be a part of the TEM Gemini Centre,  and the characterization activities in SFI FAST, working in close collaboration with project partners from NTNU and SINTEF, and with leading Norwegian and international industrial partners in the aluminium value chain.

The PhD candidate will investigate how microstructural constituents influence plastic deformation, strain localisation and ductile fracture in recycled aluminium alloys. The project aims to establish a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms governing ductility in alloys produced with increasing amounts of post-consumer scrap, where complex microstructures arise from variations in alloy chemistry, thermomechanical processing and impurity content.

The research will combine advanced electron microscopy, scanning electron microscopy and mechanical testing to characterise microstructural features across multiple length scales, including precipitates, precipitate-free zones, grain boundaries, constituent particles and deformation-induced defect structures. Particular emphasis will be placed on understanding how these microstructural constituents interact during deformation and how they affect strain localisation, damage evolution and fracture.

The project builds on previous work performed within the TEM Gemini Centre and SFI FAST and will be carried out in close collaboration with researchers in materials physics and solid mechanics at NTNU and SINTEF. The PhD candidate will work closely with experts in advanced microscopy, deformation experiments and microstructure-based modelling, contributing to the development of future recycled aluminium alloys with improved mechanical performance.

The starting date is August or September 2027. Requests for an earlier or later starting date may be considered and must be stated in the application.

Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
About SFI FAST – Future Aluminium Structures 
SFI FAST (Future Aluminium Structures) is a national Centre for Research-based Innovation (SFI) funded by the Research Council of Norway and the aluminium industry. The centre is led by NTNU in close collaboration with SINTEF and a broad consortium of 15 leading industrial partners across the aluminium value chain. SFI FAST runs from 2026 to 2033 and represents one of Norway’s most ambitious long-term research initiatives within aluminium materials, manufacturing technologies, and circular economy. 

The primary objective of SFI FAST is to establish the scientific and technological knowledge base required to enable the large-scale use of post-consumer scrap (PCS) aluminium in high-value, structural, and safety-critical products. FAST adopts a through-scale and through-process research methodology, integrating materials science, manufacturing processes, product and structural design, and lifecycle performance. 

A key outcome of SFI FAST is the development of the FAST Virtual Lab, a digital framework combining experimental data, physics-based models, and data-driven methods to support design, manufacturing, and decision-making across aluminium value chains. 

Education and competence building are central pillars of FAST. The centre will educate more than 18 PhD and postdoctoral researchers and over 100 MSc students, strengthening Norway’s international position in aluminium research and innovation. 5 PhD students started in 2026.

Please see the centre’s website: Future Aluminium Structures (FAST) - NTNU
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate degree
• Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above
• Conduct and publish high-level research in peer-reviewed journals
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions
• Contribute to popular science dissemination
• Participate in the TEM Gemini Centre and SFI FAST research groups 
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions
• Investigate how microstructural constituents such as precipitates, precipitate-free zones, grain boundaries and constituent particles influence deformation, strain localisation and ductility in recycled aluminium alloys.
• Plan and perform advanced microstructural characterisation using state-of-the-art electron microscopy and related techniques, including TEM, STEM, SEM, EBSD and diffraction-based methods.

Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria

If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• Good oral and written presentation skills in English
• Experience with experimental work within physics, nanotechnology or material science.
• Basic programming skills.
• The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.Preferred selection criteria
• Hands-on experience with materials characterisation using electron microscopy techniques, preferably (S)TEM and/or SEM/EBSD.
• Interest in microstructure-property relationships, deformation mechanisms and mechanical behaviour of metallic materials.
• Interest and experience in working with industrial problems.
• Experience with image analysis, programming or quantitative data processing (in Python) is an advantage.
• Good oral and written presentation skills in Norwegian.Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• Work independently
• Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them

• Get involved and contribute constructively with feedback
• Show curiosity and a strong motivation for the subject

Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
• Participation in a new innovative research centre, in an international work environment involving SINTEF and key industrial European partners in the aluminium value chain.
• Collaboration with leading experts in advanced material science, addressing highly relevant industrial and societal challenges for European industries.
• Training and access to state-of-the-art instruments at the TEM Gemini Centre /NORTEM Trondheim node.
• An exciting job with an important mission in society

• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)

As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Physics within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include:

• If you have finished your master’s degree, include a copy of the master's thesis.

If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).
General information

You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the Job
We have a vacancy for research position of 12 months at the Department of Geosciences (IGV) at NTNU within the group Well and Reservoir (former Reservoir Engineering and Petrophysics). The position is funded by PoreLab and organized under the Department of Geosciences. The position will be situated within the Center of Excellence PoreLab, which will give excellent opportunities for collaboration and development on a personal and scientific level. For the position as a researcher, the goal is to develop experimental proof to validate theoretical predictions for multiphase fluid flow characterization at the Darcy scale.

The researcher will work in close collaboration with associate professor Antje van der Net and professors Alex Hansen and Carl Fredrik Berg. 

Your immediate leader is the head of the department in IGV. 
Duties of the position
• The area of interest is multiphase fluid flow description at pore level using pore scale imaging. 
• The objective of the research work is to verify the newly developed theory for multiphase flow in porous media based on equilibrium thermodynamics using entropy as flow descriptor. This requires imaging of spatial fluid distribution under different flow conditions and porous media characteristics.
• The validation shall be done using experimental methods supported by numerical modelling tools. The work might require development of new experimental methodsRequired selection criteria
• Minimum a PhD in a relevant subject area STEM, preferably related to fluid mechanics and transport in porous media. 
• A strong background in thermodynamics is preferred as well as experimental experience in a fluid mechanics laboratory and imaging techniques
• Good written and oral English. Preferred selection criteria

jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Multi-Robot Informative Planning for Coastal Monitoring
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
The Department of ICT and Natural Sciences (IIR) at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) in Ålesund is opening a PhD position in distributed informative planning for teams of autonomous and remotely operated marine vehicles, with applications in coastal environmental monitoring.

Coastal waters and fjords change continuously. Pollutants spread, floating litter drifts with wind and currents, and water quality and biological activity vary across both space and time. A single vehicle can only observe a small part of such an environment at once. Teams of unmanned surface vehicles (USVs), supported by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), can cover larger areas, observe processes from several viewpoints at the same time, and respond to what they detect.

To use such teams effectively, the vehicles must build a shared and predictive picture of the environment and decide together where each of them should go next. They must do this under the real constraints of the marine environment, including limited communication, changing weather and heterogeneous vehicles.

The position is part of NTNU Ålesund’s work on ocean intelligence: collecting data about the ocean to support use cases such as monitoring of fish spawning grounds, mapping of microplastics and suspended contamination and water quality monitoring. 

The position builds on ongoing research at the department on autonomous surface vehicles, informative path planning, online mapping of spatial fields and tracking of drifting targets, which has been validated in field trials. The PhD project will extend these methods from single vehicles to cooperating teams of heterogeneous vehicles.

The research will combine theory, simulation and field experiments. Field work will be carried out in coastal waters near Ålesund with the department's fleet of USVs and UAVs.

The successful candidate will contribute to one or more of the following areas:

• Multi-robot coordination for monitoring spatially and temporally varying phenomena, such as drifting objects, pollutant plumes and evolving environmental fields, including distributed informative path and trajectory planning.
• Mobile robot sensing, mapping and active decision making for heterogeneous teams of USVs and UAVs, using methods such as model predictive control, sampling-based planning, probabilistic mapping and machine learning, under limited and intermittent communication.
• Implementation on real vehicles and validation in field experiments, including remote operation and supervision of the team
Within the scope of the project, the PhD research can be adapted to the candidate's interests and background, with emphasis on planning and control, estimation and mapping, or learning-based methods.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral training programme and successfully obtain a PhD degree.
• Conduct high-quality research within the framework described above.
• Develop, implement and test algorithms in simulation and on real vehicles.
• Plan and take part in field experiments with teams of USVs and UAVs.
• Contribute to academic publications and engage in popular science dissemination.
• Actively participate in the research group Cyber-Physical Systems Laboratory (CPS Lab).
• Engage in international academic activities, including conferences and/or research stays at partner institutions abroad.
• Take courses in relevant technical topics, comprising a minimum of 30 ECTS.Required selection criteria
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in engineering cybernetics, robotics, control engineering, marine technology, mechatronics or a closely related field. Candidates with strong backgrounds in computer science, applied mathematics or data science combined with relevant experience in robotics, optimization or machine learning will also be considered. 
• Your course of study must correspond to a five-year Norwegian course, where 120 credits have been obtained at master's level. Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position.
• You must have a strong academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker grade background, you may be considered if you can document that you are particularly suitable for a PhD education.
• You must have good programming skills, for example in Python or C++.
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's doctoral programme in Engineering Cybernetics.
• Applicants from non-English speaking countries outside Europe must present an official language test report. The acceptable tests are TOEFL, IELTS, and Cambridge Certificate in Advanced English (CAE) or Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE).
• Minimum scores are:
• TOEFL: 600 / writing 4.5 (paper-based) or 92 / writing 22 (internet-based)
• IELTS: 6.5, with no section lower than 5.5 (only Academic IELTS test accepted)
• CAE/CPE: grade B or A. 
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Experience with multi-agent or multi-robot systems, distributed optimization or distributed estimation
• Experience with informative path planning, model predictive control or sampling-based planning
• Experience with Gaussian processes or other probabilistic mapping methods
• Experience with ROS/ROS2, robotics simulators such as Gazebo, or GPU-accelerated computing
• Experience with field work, marine vehicles or drones
• Drone pilot certificate (EU A1/A3 or A2) and/or boat driving license for Norway
• Demonstrated research ability, e.g. through publications, thesis work, technical reports or open-source contributions.
• Relevant industry or applied research experience.
The research activity may lead to using sensitive information or insights into critical infrastructure that is subject to specific security restrictions. Restrictions could also include obtaining a formal security clearance according to the Norwegian Security Act. Non-Norwegian citizens can be granted clearance. However, candidates from non-EEA or non-NATO countries can not expect to obtain a security clearance.
Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to:

• Work independently and in a structured way, as well as collaboratively within an interdisciplinary team
• Communicate effectively and present and discuss your research with other professionals
• Be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed

The employment period is 3 years, with the possibility of up to 12 months additional employment related to career-enhancing activities.

jobs.description:
Roofers (Bitumen/PVC) - Bergen - Career Opportunities

Skuteviken Personell AS is seeking skilled roofers for flat roof projects in Bergen and the surrounding area. Our customers range from smaller contractors to large nationwide companies.

For the right candidates, there are good opportunities to take on more responsibility and develop into senior roles within the company.

Typical work tasks include:

• 

Installation and repair of flat roofs using bitumen and/or PVC

• 

Torch-down roofing work (experience preferred)

• 

Working according to technical drawings and building instructions

• 

Ensuring HSE compliance and high-quality standards

We offer:

• 

Competitive salary: NOK 285-315 per hour (depending on experience)

• 

Permanent full-time employment

• 

Possibility of rotation work

• 

Career development opportunities for the right candidates

• 

Coverage of daily travel costs (if more than 7.5 km from home to workplace)

• 

Free professional tools and work clothes

• 

Housing in company apartments if needed

• 

Supportive and service-oriented administration

Requirements:

• 

Minimum 2 years' experience with bitumen/asphalt and/or PVC roofing

• 

Ability to follow and understand building instructions and methods

Preferred qualifications:

• 

Torch-down roofing experience

• 

Hot work certificate (can also be obtained before starting)

• 

English or Scandinavian language skills (professional competence is most important)

Personal qualities:

• 

High work ethic

• 

Reliable and punctual

• 

Solution-oriented

Interested?

Please send your CV and application as soon as possible. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis.

jobs.occupation: Experienced Carpenters Wanted – Bergen – Join Our Team
jobs.description:
Carpenters - Bergen - Exciting Projects & Career Opportunities

Skuteviken Personell AS continues to grow and has several exciting projects in Bergen and the surrounding area. We are now looking for independent and skilled carpenters to strengthen our team.

In addition to traditional carpentry work, we also need candidates with experience in interior system installations. You do not need to be a fully qualified carpenter - practical skills and solid experience are equally valuable.

Typical work tasks include:

• 

Building exterior walls and wooden house structures

• 

Installation of walls, ceilings, doors, and windows

• 

Interior system installations (walls, ceilings, office partitions)

• 

Renovation and finishing work

• 

Reading and working from technical drawings

We offer:

• 

Competitive salary: NOK 275 - 307 per hour (depending on experience)

• 

Permanent full-time employment

• 

Varied projects - both traditional carpentry and/or system carpentry

• 

Coverage of daily travel costs (if more than 7.5 km from home to workplace)

• 

Free professional tools and work clothes

• 

Housing in company apartments if needed

• 

Supportive and service-oriented administration

• 

Career development opportunities for the right candidates

Requirements:

• 

Minimum 2 years' experience in carpentry or interior system installations

• 

Ability to read and understand technical drawings

• 

Knowledge of Scandinavian building methods is an advantage

• 

English or Scandinavian language skills (professional competence is most important)

Personal qualities:

• 

High work ethic

• 

Reliable and punctual

• 

Independent and solution-oriented

Interested?

Please send your CV and application as soon as possible. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis.
